effect: Small Bomberman in Normal Game (until reset); the password screen returns to the title
note: $C5:7287 compares the raw digits 5,6,5,6 after the checksum fails and sets $0C90=1; read at $C4:18B0 and $C6:179B (sprite set). Typed in Mesen and seen in 1-1.

US/EU $C5:4F52 also require the multitap ID ($0CEF&$1F=1, $0CE0=$40); JP and beta test only pad 5 R ($0CEE bit $10). Verified with a real press in all four: Mesen with --snes.port2.type=Multitap, emu.setInput({r=true},0,1,3) (port 2, multitap port D) on the title; no multitap: no sound test in US.

code: X in rhythm during the prologue
effect: Start the next Normal Game with 9 lives instead of 5
note: $C5:6698: 48 X presses in a row, each 7-9 frames after the last (a ~7.5 Hz turbo works); a gap of 32 frames or a wrong interval resets. Sets $0C8F, which $C5:5106 turns into 9 lives. The prologue only plays in JP (demo table $C5:501F); in US/EU/beta it is unreachable without a cheat (PAR 7E00A433). Verified natively in JP and with the $A4 redirect in US (40 presses: 5 lives, 60: 9).

code: Start a Normal Game or password with controller 2
effect: Player 2 plays alone with the lives; Player 1 shows PRESS START
note: $C5:5128 / $C5:7350 test controller 2's new presses ($0CFA & $1080 = A or Start) and give the lives to $0DBD instead of $0D7D. Checked on the title in US, JP and the beta (tools/sb1/test_p2_start.lua).

code: Game over on a boss stage (x-8)
effect: The CONTINUE screen shows an x-7 code, never a boss code
note: $C5:6F23 steps $0D17/$0D16 back one stage when the stage digit is 8, then encodes. Game over at 5-8 showed 2234 (5-7). The x-8 codes in GameFAQs are still valid passwords.

effect: Seven music tracks the game never plays: a different take on the world 1 theme, four tunes that start past their intro, and two copies of the world jingles
note: Every track request goes through $C3:002C (Y = track), fed by the stage/scene table $C3:2F83, the jingle tables $C4:1874 and $C4:6C04, a few constants and the sound test's 18-entry list at $C7:07C9. None of them gives 03, 05, 09, 13, 15, 28 or 29; only the debug menu's BGM NO. plays them. 03 is another arrangement of the world 1 theme (02), denser and with parts an octave apart. 05, 09, 13 and 15 are tracks 04, 08, 12 and 14 starting past their intros. 28 and 29 copy the two per-world jingles note for note and sit in the demo's song set.
